cover.title: Time-Series Demo
cover.categories: Visual Design, Front-end Development, Data Visualization

header: Time-series data is hard to picture in the abstract. For Timescale’s marketing, I designed a demo that makes it concrete: a dashboard for an energy site, where a steady stream of sensor readings becomes something anyone can read at a glance. I did the visual design and part of the front-end build.
seo_description: Senior Product Design Case Study: Translating complex database architecture into human centered design systems and real time visual narratives.

media.name: index.html
media.title: A static version of the demo. The original ran on Shell’s real field data.

layout.title: Background
text: Time-series data is any measurement recorded over time, like a sensor reading every second. On its own, that’s an abstract idea, and most people only care once they see what it lets you do. So instead of explaining the concept, we showed it in the real world. Shell let us use actual sensor data from its sites in the field, and the demo turned it into a dashboard where spotting a pattern early could prevent a failure, or an environmental incident.

layout.title: Designing for a glance
text: I organized the dashboard around the questions an operator asks first. Is the well on target? The top shows total production against its goal, with a single progress bar. Is anything about to fail? In Pressure Analytics, every well is plotted against a safety threshold, and any well that crosses it turns red. Out of thirteen wells, the three near the limit stand out immediately.
